key_insight: Under realistic, physically constrained NWP errors, sequence models are more robust than a strong tabular baseline because they better filter noise and shift reliance toward stable history and physical priors.
engineering_relevance: For PV forecasting systems, robustness should be evaluated alongside nominal accuracy and latency so model choice reflects behavior under forecast uncertainty, not just clean-input performance.
method: Simulated PV power as a controlled response to isolate uncertainty propagation from plant-level confounders.
Applied dynamic NWP perturbations with state-dependent, heteroscedastic errors tied to clear-sky conditions and Erbs-consistent radiation reconstruction.
Compared six models, including PatchTST, GRU, N-HITS, and LightGBM, using accuracy, robustness, and latency plus SHAP/IG interpretation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports six models tested under dynamic NWP perturbations with medium-to-high disturbance regimes and a Pareto analysis spanning clean accuracy, robustness, and computational latency.
watch_item: Robustness conclusions are based on virtual PV power and simulated NWP perturbations, so transfer to a specific plant or operational forecast pipeline still needs site-level validation.
paper_title: Robustness of Deep Learning Models for PV Power Forecasting under NWP Forecast Errors: A Spatiotemporal and Physically Interpretable Analysis
